Yusuf’s classroom had twenty desks, one blackboard, and a very naughty class hamster named Buttons.

Buttons lived in a cage near the window. He liked sunflower seeds, paper scraps, and escaping when no one was looking.

One afternoon, after art class, Yusuf stayed back to pick up crayons. Under the last desk, he found a small purple diary.

It had a silver star on the cover and one word written neatly:

Private

Yusuf picked it up.

Just then, Buttons escaped from his cage and ran across the floor with a piece of tissue in his mouth.

“Buttons!” Yusuf laughed.

He caught the hamster near the bookshelf and put him back.

Then Yusuf looked at the diary again.

He liked solving mysteries.

Who owned it? What was inside? Why was it locked?

His friends Sam and Noor came in.

“What did you find?” Sam asked.

“A diary,” Yusuf said.

Noor’s eyes grew wide. “Open it!”

“I can’t,” Yusuf said. “It says private.”

Sam bent closer. “Maybe there is a name inside.”

Yusuf held the diary tightly.

Then Noor whispered, “Maybe it belongs to Anya. She has been quiet all week.”

Yusuf looked toward Anya’s empty desk.

Maybe the diary explained why she was sad. Maybe reading it would help.

His fingers touched the tiny lock.

Then he looked at the word again.

Private

Yusuf thought about his own notebook at home. It had drawings, silly poems, and one page where he had written, “I am scared of big dogs.”

He would not want anyone reading that.

So he walked to Mrs. Mehta’s desk.

“I found this diary,” he said. “I did not open it.”

Mrs. Mehta smiled. “Thank you, Yusuf.”

Later, Yusuf saw Mrs. Mehta return the diary to Anya.

Anya came to him at lunch.

“Did you read it?” she asked softly.

Yusuf shook his head. “No.”

“Did anyone else?”

“No,” Yusuf said. “I kept it safe.”

Anya smiled a small smile. “Thank you.”

Yusuf still did not know what was inside the diary.

But that was okay.

Some things are not mysteries to solve.

Some things are trusts to protect.
